The accomplishments come from the ledger (`docs/objectives.md`) and settled duels: a rubbing leaving a source is collected, one leaving a cache is a cache claimed, one moving between players is a theft and a loss, one going into a cache is a loss; a settled win or draw counts for both fighters, a cancelled duel for neither. The results (the flow's) are synced to everyone once, shown until players leave (Back to lobby returns to the landing page), and recorded in the process's outcome list (`recordedOutcomes`).

- **Seeds.** One private master secret per match (32 bytes of `node:crypto`'s `randomBytes`). Each system's seed is `HMAC-SHA-256(secret, "pirate-sea-race/seed/v1/" + system)`, its first four bytes: `world`, `ledger`, `final-socket`, `intel`, `ruins`, `fruit` (the fruit deal), and each duel's `duel:<n>`. No raw seed feeds two systems and none reads the match code; unit and integration tests check both.

-- **Test hooks** (`MatchTuning.testHooks`, off by default, never set by an entry point): `injectFault()` makes the next world tick throw (an `aborted` ending), `pauseAfterTick(tick)` / `resumeWorld()` stop the clock after a tick so a test lines an input up with an exact tick (a grapple landing on a claim's completion tick, a claim completing on the deadline tick), and `injectFlowReports(reports)` adds reports to the flow's next step (a ghost player's, to show they are dropped).

+- **Test hooks** (`MatchTuning.testHooks`, off by default, never set by an entry point): `injectFault()` makes the next world tick throw (an `aborted` ending), `pauseAfterTick(tick)` / `resumeWorld()` stop the clock after a tick so a test lines an input up with an exact tick (a grapple landing on a claim's completion tick, a claim completing on the deadline tick), `injectFlowReports(reports)` adds reports to the flow's next step (a ghost player's, to show they are dropped), and `testBuyRumor(id, request)` with `stepWorldTicks(n)` lines targeted rumor requests up with exact ticks while the clock is paused.

- **Coverage.** `docs/match-online-coverage.md` lists every room-level and UI branch this feature added or changed, each with the test that fails without it. `recordedOutcomes` keeps only the latest 64 (`outcomes.ts`).

- **Into duels.** `openSeaDuel` passes `kitOf` for both fighters to the `DuelMachine`, which creates the frame-0 state with them and syncs them in the lobby. Both clients build the same state from the seed and the kits, so the per-frame hashes cover them. No rule clears a meal, so the kit survives a lost duel.

- **Browser.** `fruitPanel.ts` holds the HUD's kit and pedestal lines, the panel's view model and the `FruitPanel` controller. `pageKeys.ts` routes a keydown to one panel at a time and skips keys typed into text fields. `arenaDrawing.ts` turns `fighterTells` into the arena's shapes: bolts, smoke screens, the obscured startup flash, the reappearance, and threats only for striking moves. The arena reports `data-bolts`, `data-zones` and `data-tells`. The branch table is `docs/fruit-kits-online-coverage.md`.

+- **Delivery.** Every intel message kind reaches players (`intelMessageOf`, `apps/server/src/intel.ts`, copies each field by name): the reveals as `reveal` messages as before, and every lead (`rumor`, `carrier-sighting`, `no-lead`, `rumor-stale`, `rumor-resolved`) as a `journal` message to its one player (protocol v10). None names a player or a rubbing, or the position of a source, cache or ship.

+- **The journal log.** Intel's own journal keeps neither sightings, no-lead notices nor what followed a stale rumor, so the room logs every lead each player receives (`JournalLog`: the last 24 entries, each with its kind, type, target name, reason, tick and status; a stale entry is linked to the next lead of its type, whatever its reason). It is in the player's own `status` (`journal`, JSON), with `knownIslands` (islands had in sight, by the ruin markers' sight rule, or moored at, each one's unlocked state as last seen, and solved by them) and `rumorOffers` (`targetedRumorAvailability` per missing type), so a reconnecting player reads it back.

+- **Targeted rumors** (`buy-rumor`, 8 a second). A decided (player, request id) is answered from the room's record first (`RumorBook`: every bought id with its lead, the last 16 refusals). Otherwise, in play, it waits: a pending id's retry merges into it, a third is refused `busy`. The purchase runs in the reveal step, last in the world tick: at most one request per player per tick, oldest first; refused unless the ship is moored at a dock on this tick (and not waiting to respawn), the ledger has the player connected, out of any duel and with the price, and `targetedRumorAvailability` offers a lead; then `stepIntel` under `<player>:<client id>`; `purchase` only for a `rumor` or `sighting` outcome (a refusal there throws: the match faults); every other outcome is one recorded refusal, uncharged. Each answer (`rumor-result`) goes to its sender only.

+- **Browser.** M opens the journal (Escape closes it; Tab and Shift+Tab move among its buttons, Enter or Space presses one; the helm stays live). It lists the rumors newest first with their reasons, stale ones greyed with their replacement, the known islands, the collected types and the kit with its §9 description, and a Buy button per missing type (available, covered, no lead, not at a dock, too little gold, or waiting). A toast announces each new lead once. The sea draws the 3 × 3 sector borders, and names the sector the ship enters, only while the journal is open or a sector lead is active. The branch table is `docs/intel-online-coverage.md`.

- **Duel room.** `DuelRoom` (room name `duel`) holds one duel, a `DuelMachine`: two players, or one in practice against a server-side dummy (player two, `idle` or `guard`). It is admitted like a match, by the same code in `admission.ts`: a one-time create token, `onAuth` before any seat, the room's own check, `filterBy(['code', 'createToken'])`, no token in the listing. The countdown (180 frames) starts once every seat is taken; the machine probes round trips during it, chooses the shared input delay 30 frames before the end, then steps `DuelAuthority` at 60 Hz, which the room's `setFixedTimestep` drives. Inputs go through `DuelInputGate`, which admits them through the same `InputAdmission` as the world's `InputGate` (the rate window and the protocol validation: 128 bytes, 60 a second of room ticks, increasing sequence, 30 frames of lead), so the two cannot drift, and counts its drops. Frame bundles and probes are Colyseus messages; the lobby is a small Schema state. A drop keeps the seat for 10 s (`allowReconnection`); leaving, or staying away, forfeits, decided at the next frame boundary (two forfeits on one frame: no winner). The rules and rates are in `docs/duel.md`.

11:The race is for rubbings (§4; the slice plays Sun and Moon, two sealed sources on each island). Each island's rubbings are locked behind its ruin (§3): moored at its dock, press R to read the clue (six carved tablets whose hints give three symbols in order, or a 4 × 4 grid to walk from start to goal) and enter the answer with the keys or clicks. The first solver unlocks the island for everyone, and every solver earns 40 gold once; a wrong answer locks you out for three seconds. Then keep holding E: after six seconds you collect its rubbing of a type you lack (the HUD shows what the island holds, only while you are moored there, and the hold's progress). Win a duel at sea and, within five seconds, press 1 or 2 (or click) to steal one of the loser's types you lack, with 20 % of their gold (the rarest type is taken if you do not choose; a draw moves nothing). The purse beside the game shows your gold, your rubbings and what the last duel took or gave, and whether the winner chose it or the default took it. A player who drops keeps their seat, ship and rubbings for 60 seconds (a fighter away from a duel for ten seconds forfeits it); one who never returns, or quits, leaves a recovery cache at a dock, a chest others see when in sight. Moor there and hold E to claim one rubbing of a type you lack.
13:Fruit powers join the race (§9). Four fruit pedestals, two Ember and two Smoke, stand at island docks; a pedestal in sight shows whether it still holds its fruit. Moored at a pedestal's dock, press F to read its kit: the two specials and what they're good for. Hold F for three seconds to eat it. Letting go, casting off, a grapple or a disconnect stops the meal, and if two captains finish together the fruit goes to one of them. The kit replaces your two specials (U, I) in every duel at sea for the rest of the match, even after a defeat. A duel shows both fighters' kits. The arena draws Ember's flame bolts and Smoke's smoke screens, and a fighter inside a screen still shows a startup flash, its position and its health.
15:The standalone duel (the combat spike, §18 stage 1) runs beside it: "Create duel" makes a 1v1 duel whose code the second browser enters under "Join duel", and "Practice" fights a server-side dummy (idle or guarding). After a three-second countdown both browsers predict the fight with the shared duel simulation and roll back to the server's inputs (`docs/duel.md`). Keys (§8): WASD or the arrows move (hold back to guard), J light, K heavy, U and I specials, Shift dash, J and K together throw. The HUD shows both health bars, stamina, the round clock, the connection line (round trip, input delay, corrections) and the result; "Show hitboxes" draws hurtboxes and active hitboxes.

content.text:
Rumors, sightings, stale leads, purchases and the journal are all in, and all five checks pass. Nothing is committed, as instructed; the changes are uncommitted in this worktree, and the completion file is written.

## What was built
- **Delivery:** the room now sends players every intel message kind. The reveals keep their `reveal` messages, and every lead goes to its one player as a new `journal` message (protocol version 10).
- **Journal log:** the room keeps each player's last 24 leads, including sightings and no-lead notices, with a stale entry linked to whatever lead of its type came next. It lives in the player's private status along with known islands and rumor offers, so a reconnecting player gets it back.
- **Targeted rumors:** these follow the settled order:
  - A request id the room has already decided is answered from its record first.
  - Otherwise the request waits: a retry of a pending id is merged, and a third waiting request is refused `busy`.
  - At most one request per player per tick is processed, last in the tick.
  - Checks, in order: moored at a dock on this tick, the ledger's state, then an available lead.
  - `stepIntel` runs under `<player>:<id>`, and `purchase` is called only when a lead is delivered. A refused charge there throws, and the match faults.
- **Browser:**
  - M opens and closes the journal and Escape closes it. Tab moves between its buttons, and the ship can still be steered while it's open.
  - It has Buy buttons, a toast for each new lead, and sector borders shown only while the journal is open or a sector lead is active.
- **Carried from the fruit reviews:** all five are done and tested, including the fruit panel staying open to show why eating stopped, and ignoring F's auto-repeat.

## Checks run (after the last change)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| `npm run test:unit` | 1387 / 1387 |
| `npm run test:integration` | 136 / 136, **192 s** of the 300 s budget (the suite was about 185 s before this feature) |
| `npm run build` | pass, smoke test passed |
| Playwright, full suite | 15 / 15 in 407 s; `check-report` accepts it |
| `journal.spec.ts` alone | passes; `check-report` accepts it |

## Branch table
`docs/intel-online-coverage.md` has 191 rows: 174 tested, 8 equivalent, 9 removed, and no untested ones. Building it found real gaps, which I fixed:
- **Dead code removed:** a revision counter nothing read, and three redundant empty-string checks.
- **Missing tests added:** offers leaving out held types, and known-island order.
- **Flake fixed:** the new browser scenario could fail whenever the host's random spawn slot was already in the north-west sector, since no new sector name ever showed. It now moves the ship to the hub first, and passed 4 of 4 repeats. I reran every browser-level mutation after that fix.

## Decisions to review
- **Changed existing test:** a §16 wire check in `rubbings.test.ts` assumed the guest's frames never contain "sun". The guest's own journal and offers now legitimately name the Sun it lacks. The check now scans state frames with only those two string forms removed. Please confirm it still guards what it meant to.
- **Version tests:** the old "protocol v9" tests now assert version ≥ 9; the new journal tests assert exactly 10.
- **Refusal reasons:** a player waiting to respawn gets `not-at-dock` even if the ship still sits at a dock. Requests before the match starts or after it ends get `not-in-play`, which isn't recorded.
- **Status format:** the journal, known islands and offers travel as strings (JSON, and `type:offer` pairs), not nested Schema collections.
- **Sighting status:** sighting and no-lead entries stay `active`, because the design takes "resolved" only from `rumor-resolved`.

## Files
- **New:**
  - `apps/server/src/intel.ts` and its test
  - `packages/protocol/src/journal.ts` and its test
  - `apps/web/src/journal.ts` and its test
  - `tests/integration/intel.test.ts`, `tests/integration/intelSightings.test.ts`
  - `tests/e2e/journal.spec.ts`
  - `docs/intel-online-coverage.md`
- **Modified:**
  - server: `MatchRoom.ts`, `schema.ts`, `server.ts`, `index.ts`
  - protocol: `index.ts`, `version.ts`, `testPlacement.ts`
  - web: `index.html`, `style.css`, `main.ts`, `pageKeys.ts`, `fruitPanel.ts`, `seaScene.ts`, `matchView.ts`, `palette.ts`
  - test tools: `headlessClient.ts`
  - tests: `fruits`, `ruins`, `ledgerSeed` and `rubbings` integration tests, `fruit.test.ts`, `web.test.ts`, `protocol.test.ts`
  - docs: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/objectives.md`, `README.md`
